title: Core ideas in computer science
description: How computers store information, run algorithms, and where their limits lie.

ideas.title: Bits and binary
ideas.summary: Everything a computer stores, from numbers to text to pictures, is a pattern of bits, each a 0 or a 1.
links: How a computer runs a program

items.q: How many bits are in a byte?
How many different values can n bits represent?
How is the decimal number 10 written in binary?
What is the largest value an unsigned 8-bit number can hold?
Who founded information theory with the 1948 paper "A Mathematical Theory of Communication"?
items.a: Claude Shannon

ideas.title: Algorithms and their cost
ideas.summary: An algorithm is a precise step-by-step procedure, and big O notation says how its cost grows with its input.

items.q: In computer science, what does big O notation describe?
items.a: An asymptotic upper bound on how a cost, such as running time or memory use, grows with input size

items.q: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n items?
items.a: O(log n)

items.q: What is the worst-case time complexity of merge sort on n items?
items.a: O(n log n)

items.q: In programming, what is recursion?
items.a: A function solving a problem by calling itself on smaller versions of it

ideas.title: Data structures
ideas.summary: The way data is arranged in memory decides which operations on it are fast and which are slow.

items.q: Which data structure removes items in last-in, first-out order?
items.a: A stack

items.q: Which data structure removes items in first-in, first-out order?
items.a: A queue

items.q: What is the average time complexity of looking up a key in a hash table?
items.a: O(1): constant time on average

items.q: What is the main advantage of an array over a linked list?
items.a: Constant-time access to any element by its index

ideas.title: Computation and its limits
ideas.summary: One simple abstract machine can compute anything computable, yet some problems no program can ever solve.

items.q: Which mathematician described, in 1936, the abstract machine that defines what can be computed?
items.a: Alan Turing

items.q: In computer science, what is the halting problem?
items.a: Deciding whether any given program will eventually stop; Turing proved no algorithm can always do it

items.q: What does it mean to call a programming language Turing complete?
items.a: It can compute anything that a Turing machine can compute

items.q: What does the unsolved P versus NP question ask?
items.a: Whether every problem whose solution can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly

ideas.title: How a computer runs a program
ideas.summary: A processor fetches instructions from memory and carries them out one at a time, with software built in layers.

items.q: What is the central idea of the stored-program, or von Neumann, design of a computer?
items.a: Program instructions and data are held in the same memory

items.q: In programming, what does a compiler do?
items.a: It translates source code into another language or representation, often machine code or bytecode

items.q: What is the job of a computer's operating system?
items.a: It manages the hardware and shares it among the running programs

items.q: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when both of its inputs are 1?
items.a: The AND gate

ideas.title: The internet and encryption
ideas.summary: The internet moves data as small addressed packets, and mathematics keeps that data private on the way.

items.q: What are the small addressed units called into which data is split to travel across the internet?
items.a: Packets

items.q: What does the Domain Name System (DNS) do?
items.a: It translates domain names into IP addresses

items.q: In public-key cryptography, which key encrypts a message to a person and which key decrypts it?
items.a: Their public key encrypts it; only their private key decrypts it
